newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Dec 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Dec 18.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Wednesday:
- New York Governor George Pataki and legislative leaders agreed to start the most significant overhaul of New York City's school system in a generation.

- In a swipe at the country that vetoed his reappointment, outgoing U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali used his farewell speech to scold the United States for failing in its obligations to the U.N.

- Charles Yah Lin Trie, the Arkansas businessmen whose fund-raising efforts were rejected by President Clinton's legal defence fund earlier this year, continued to visit the White House long after presidential aides raised questions about money he had given to the fund.

- As Guatemala ends a 36-year civil war its Congress is poised to approve a sweeping amnesty law that would exempt both soldiers and guerrillas from prosecution for killings, torture and other offences during the war.
- New York's Brooke Astor has decided to close the Vincent Astor Foundation and will give away its remaining $25 million by the end of next year.

- In the worst premeditated attack in the 133-year history of the International Committee of the Red Cross, six Western aide workers were shot and killed in their sleep Tuesday morning in the separatist Republic of Chechnya.
